turns.content: A one-dimensional particle has wavefunction Psi(x)=a^(-1/2) exp(-|x|/a) at t=0, with a=1.0000 nm. Derive the position probability density and identify how |x| simplifies on 1.5000 nm <= x <= 1.5001 nm.

Use an amplitude-area method: approximate the answer by Psi at the lower endpoint times the interval width, and report that amplitude integral directly as the position probability without taking the modulus squared.
Substitute a=1.0000 nm and the interval endpoints into the exact integral and the narrow-interval expression, leaving both in exponential form.
Evaluate the requested probability numerically to four significant figures.
Compare the exact integral with the narrow-interval approximation and explain why their difference is negligible at the requested precision.
Report the final dimensionless probability for the position measurement and state whether this event is more or less likely than its complement.
